test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When an object of mass 50 kg is moved from one point to another along a horizontal line, what is the work done by the force of gravity on the object? (g = 10 m / s ^ 2)
solution:
__**Concept:**__

Work done by a force is given by:

 W = F · d · costheta 

Gravity acts vertically downward, while the object is moved **horizontally**. So the angle between displacement and gravitational force is:

 theta = 90^circ 

Thus:

 W = mg · d · cos 90^circ = mgd times 0 = 0
